transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Um, yeah—so I came in because I feel like I just cannot keep things organized, especially between my schoolwork and this little accessories shop I’m trying to manage. It’s like there are too many categories of things at once—my supplies, due dates, receipts, assignment notes, little product ideas, all of it—and somehow they all just end up in piles.

Like, I’ll have a stack of papers for school next to beads or packaging stuff, then a receipt I need to keep gets mixed in with notes for an assignment, and then I don’t know what’s urgent anymore. I’ll sit down to do something and I’m just staring at everything thinking, “Okay, what am I supposed to do first?” And then I waste so much time just trying to figure out where things are or what the next step is.

It’s been really frustrating because I’m not trying to ignore things. I do care about school, and I do care about the shop, but I feel like I can’t keep both systems running at the same time. Everything feels scattered and I’m kind of overwhelmed by it.

Do you find it hard to stay organized or focused on tasks in other parts of your life, like keeping your room tidy, following through with plans, or even just finishing a conversation without getting distracted?

Yeah, mostly with the organization side, especially when it’s school and my little shop happening at the same time. It’s like I can sort of handle one thing for a minute, but once there are supplies and due dates and receipts and assignment notes all in the same space, everything just starts blending together.

I’ll put something down thinking, “Okay, I’ll remember this is important,” and then ten minutes later it’s under packaging stuff or mixed into school papers. Then I sit there looking at these piles like I’m supposed to just know what comes first, but I don’t. I’ll be like, “Do I answer this assignment thing, do I sort the beads, do I find that receipt, do I check a due date?” And then I get stuck just trying to figure out the order instead of actually doing the task.

So, yeah, it’s not that I don’t want to do it or I don’t care. I just feel like I can’t keep the different parts organized at the same time, and then focusing on any one thing gets harder because everything around it feels messy and urgent.

Does this difficulty with staying organized and managing tasks happen in other areas of your life, like at home, with personal responsibilities, or even socially, or does it only seem to happen when you're balancing school and the shop?

I guess the main place I really notice it is when school and the shop overlap. Like, that’s where it becomes really obvious and stressful, because I’m trying to keep track of schoolwork and then also all the little shop things at the same time, and they don’t stay separate in my head or in my room.

It’s not even one big dramatic thing, it’s just constant little things—my supplies are out, then there are due dates I wrote down somewhere, receipts I’m supposed to keep, assignment notes, maybe packaging stuff, and somehow they all become these piles. And then once it’s in piles, I can’t tell what pile is “school,” what pile is “shop,” what’s urgent, what can wait. I’ll start out thinking I’m going to sit down and do an assignment, but then I see shop supplies or a receipt, and I’m like, wait, am I supposed to deal with that first? Or I’ll try to work on the shop and then remember there was a due date, but I don’t know where I wrote it down.

So I’d say it’s mostly when I’m balancing those two things. That’s what made me come in, honestly, because I feel like I cannot get them organized at the same time, and once everything is mixed together, I just kind of freeze and don’t know what to do first.
Can you think of a time when you were only managing one area of your life, like just school or just your personal space, where you still found it hard to stay organized or focused on tasks?

I’m trying to think… honestly, the clearest example is still when school and the shop are both happening, because that’s when it gets really bad. Like if it’s just one thing, I can sometimes sort of keep it together for a while, or at least it doesn’t feel as impossible.

But the reason I came in is that when I’m trying to manage my schoolwork and the little accessories shop at the same time, everything just collapses into the same mess. My supplies, due dates, receipts, assignment notes—like all these different things that are supposed to have their own places—end up in piles together. And then I don’t know what I’m looking at anymore. I’ll be sitting there thinking, okay, is this pile something for school, or is it shop stuff, or is there something urgent buried in there?

And then I get stuck on what to do first. Like, I don’t even get to the actual task because I’m trying to figure out whether I should find a due date, clean up supplies, keep track of a receipt, or start an assignment. So… I guess with just one area it’s not as obvious to me, but when those two overlap, that’s when I really feel like I can’t get organized.
Looking back, were you already having trouble staying organized or managing tasks like this when you were younger, maybe even as far back as grade school?

Yeah… actually, when I think about it, there were signs when I was little. My mom still has some of my elementary school notes from teachers, and they weren’t really about me not understanding the work. It was more like, “She’s out of her seat again,” or “She talks before being called on,” things like that.

I remember my mom showing me one where it basically said I would rush through group activities, even if I knew what we were supposed to do. Like I understood the assignment, but I’d kind of jump ahead or blurt things out or move around instead of waiting my turn. At the time I don’t think anyone made it sound like a huge issue, more like I was just too excited or needed reminders, but looking back it does feel like it was already there in grade school.
Do you often feel restless, have trouble staying seated, or feel like you need to be moving or doing something all the time, especially when you're trying to focus on a task?

Yeah, definitely. It’s kind of hard to explain because it’s not always like I’m literally getting up and running around, but my body feels… busy, I guess? Like buzzing inside.

Especially if I’m supposed to sit still and focus on something or listen to someone talk for a while, it feels like there’s this pressure to move. I’ll be sitting there, but I’m not really still. I feel like I need to shift around or do something with my body, even if I’m not actually going anywhere. It’s almost uncomfortable to just sit and listen without moving, like my brain is trying to pay attention but my body is saying, “No, we need to be doing something.”

So yes, I do feel restless a lot, especially in those situations where I’m expected to be still and just focus.
Have you noticed these same difficulties with staying focused or feeling restless in other settings, like at home, with friends, or during activities that aren’t related to school or your shop?

Yeah, it’s not just school or the shop. I notice it in regular situations too, especially if I’m supposed to just sit there and listen. Like at home, if someone is talking to me for a while, or even if I’m trying to watch something that isn’t super grabbing my attention, I feel like I’m physically still but not really still, if that makes sense.

It’s like this buzzing feeling in my body, like I need to move somehow. I might not actually get up and go anywhere, but inside it feels like I’m being pushed to shift around or do something with my hands or change position. And the more I’m supposed to be sitting quietly, the more noticeable it gets. It’s not always dramatic from the outside, but to me it feels really uncomfortable, like my body is saying, “move, move, move,” even when I know I’m supposed to stay put and pay attention.
